title: Depth of a module killed by an ideal is the same over the quotient ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ an ideal, and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $IM=0$, so that $M$ is a finite module over the Noetherian local ring $\bar R=R/I$, with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/I$, by $(r\bmod I)\cdot m=rm$. Then the depth of $M$ as an $R$-module equals the depth of $M$ as an $\bar R$-module: $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\bar{\mathfrak m}}(M)$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. In particular (for $M=R/I$) the depth of the local ring $R/I$ equals the depth of $R/I$ as an $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AUK (lemma-depth-goes-down-finite, line 18048) applied to the finite ring map $R\to R/I$, whose only maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m/I$ and for which $N_{\mathfrak m/I}=N$ as $R/I$ is local. Tag verified in tags/tags: 0AUK,algebra-lemma-depth-goes-down-finite

proof.text: Write $\bar R=R/I$ and let $\pi:R\to\bar R$ be the quotient map. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure] makes $\bar R$ local with maximal ideal $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\pi(\mathfrak m)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. If $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ generate $M$ over $R$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], they generate it over $\bar R$ too: $r m_j=\pi(r)m_j$ because $IM=0$. Thus both depths in the statement are defined for the same finite module.

source.place: Algebra, Section Tag 07BH (section-local-rings), Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), and Lemma Tag 0AUK (lemma-depth-goes-down-finite), quotient-map case

proof.text: For any list $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in\mathfrak m$, put $\bar f_j=\pi(f_j)\in\bar{\mathfrak m}$. For every $i$, the submodule $(f_1,\ldots,f_i)M$ equals $(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_i)M$, because each $f_j$ and $\bar f_j$ act identically on $M$. On the common quotient, multiplication by $f_{i+1}$ is the same endomorphism as multiplication by $\bar f_{i+1}$. Their injectivity conditions and the condition that the final quotient is nonzero therefore agree. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ is $M$-regular over $R$ if and only if $(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_r)$ is $M$-regular over $\bar R$. Conversely every sequence in $\bar{\mathfrak m}=\pi(\mathfrak m)$ has lifts in $\mathfrak m$, so the two collections of possible regular-sequence lengths coincide.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence), applied to the quotient map in Lemma Tag 0AUK (lemma-depth-goes-down-finite)

proof.text: The submodules $\mathfrak mM$ and $\bar{\mathfrak m}M$ also coincide. If this common submodule is $M$, both depths are $\infty$ by clause (2) of [def-weil-pbc-depth], including $M=0$. Otherwise clause (1) of that definition expresses each depth as the supremum of the regular-sequence lengths in its maximal ideal; these sets of lengths agree by Step 2. Hence $\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\bar{\mathfrak m}}(M)$. For $M=R/I$, the $R$-action is the quotient action and the depth of the local ring $\bar R$ is, by the same definition, the depth of $\bar R$ as its own module. This gives the final assertion.
